A_and_B_are_related_by_the_operator.reading: A is the unit-action scale with the operator carried separately; B absorbs the operator. Both routes give total hbar_q^2. So which convention a quantity takes is decided by what hbar_q power the quantity itself already carries -- not by taste.

why_the_extensive_term_is_still_unpinned.the_quantity: log Z(3A) = 3A log(1+q_0^2), the Markov-trace normaliser
why_the_extensive_term_is_still_unpinned.its_hbar_q_content: ZERO -- log(1+q_0^2) = 0.80292155 is O(1), not small. In hbar_q units it is 8.10363, not a clean power.
why_the_extensive_term_is_still_unpinned.its_Hecke_level: H_3A -- which indexes to convention B
why_the_extensive_term_is_still_unpinned.its_operator_class: NONE OF THE REGISTERED ONES. It is neither Delta_NF (A) nor a trace DIFFERENCE (B) nor a mass assembly (C). It is the logarithm of a partition function.
why_the_extensive_term_is_still_unpinned.consequence: Hecke level points at B, hbar_q content points at A, and they differ by 5.35064x. The registry does not adjudicate, so 'the extensive term is short by N' has no determinate N: it is 1.57, 8.38 or 12.84 depending on a choice the corpus has not made and, per convention D, cannot derive.

data.verdict: qou-59j5 ANSWERED: NO. E_0 is not derivable. derivation_chain's own registry calls convention A a 'closed-form algebraic substitution from CAL-1 m_e + CAL-2 q_0', the sole derivation attempt (convention D, LP dual) is a recorded negative finding with y_0^* m_e a factor of 21.8 from the target, and convention C is flagged a discipline violation. Moreover the problem is not the two-scale tension I described but a four-convention registry spanning 256x whose rungs are 1/hbar_q^2 = 102x apart, and log Z(3A) matches no registered operator class, so the registry cannot even select among A and B for it. STOP QUOTING MAGNITUDE DEFICITS FOR THE EXTENSIVE TERM.
